title: Buttermilk Scones
description: Tall, tender scones with a soft crumb and a faint tang from the buttermilk, on the table in half an hour. A light hand and a hot oven are all they ask for.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and put a large baking tray inside to heat up.
steps.tip: A hot tray gives the scones an immediate burst of heat from below, which helps them rise straight up.

steps.text: Sift the flour, baking powder and salt into a large bowl. Add the butter and rub it in with your fingertips until the mixture looks like fine breadcrumbs with a few pea-sized pieces left. Stir in the sugar.

Make a well in the middle and pour in the buttermilk. Mix quickly with a table knife, cutting through the mixture, until it just comes together into a soft, slightly sticky dough. If dry flour remains in the bottom of the bowl, add another tablespoon of buttermilk.
steps.tip: Stop mixing the moment it holds together. Every extra stir develops gluten and makes for a tougher scone.

steps.text: Tip the dough onto a lightly floured worktop and fold it over on itself two or three times until it is just smooth. Pat it out with your hands to a round about 3cm thick; do not use a rolling pin.
Dip a 6cm round cutter in flour and stamp out the scones, pressing straight down without twisting. Gently press the trimmings together and cut again; you should get 8 in total.
steps.tip: Twisting the cutter seals the edges and the scones will rise lopsided.

steps.text: Brush just the tops with beaten egg, keeping it off the sides. Arrange on the hot tray and bake for 12–15 minutes, until well risen and golden.
Cool on a wire rack for a few minutes. Serve warm or at room temperature, split by hand, with jam and clotted cream.

tips: Keep the butter and buttermilk cold and work fast, so the butter stays in small pieces until it reaches the oven.
Scones are at their best within a few hours of baking. Day-old ones revive well after 5 minutes in a 160°C oven.

substitutions.use: 170ml whole milk mixed with 2 tsp lemon juice
substitutions.note: leave to stand for 5 minutes until slightly thickened

substitutions.use: 75g sultanas as well as the sugar
substitutions.note: stirred in before the buttermilk for fruit scones

storage: Best eaten on the day. Freeze once cooled for up to 3 months, then defrost and warm through in the oven.
author: Simmer
